title: The US Government Launched 3 Previously Unreported Investigations of Polymarket Trades
gist: FOIA'd CFTC voting records show chairman Michael Selig authorized three previously unreported enforcement investigations in May and July 2026 into suspected insider trading on Polymarket contracts covering Biden's pardons, Iran, and Google's Year in Search rankings, each opened weeks after a press report rather than from internal surveillance. The pattern arrives as Polymarket, valued at $21 billion in a round led by Donald Trump Jr.'s 1789 Capital, faces its own reported CFTC probe and as two arrested traders argue prediction-market trades are betting and not subject to commodities law.

insights.claim: CFTC chairman Michael Selig approved orders in early May, late May and July 2026 opening three separate private investigations into suspected insider trading on Polymarket event contracts covering Biden pardons, Iran, and Google's 2025 Year in Search Ranking.
insights.speaker: Kate Knibbs
insights.so_what: Three concurrent enforcement tracks in a single quarter show prediction-market insider trading is now a standing CFTC workstream, raising the compliance and surveillance cost baseline for the sector.
insights.locator: The US government launched at least three

insights.claim: Each investigation order followed a media report by a matter of weeks — the pardon probe came after an NPR story on a trader who netted over $300,000, and the Iran probe came two weeks after a 60 Minutes report.
insights.speaker: Kate Knibbs
insights.so_what: Enforcement keyed to news cycles means headline risk, not trading data, is the best predictor of the next probe — monitor investigative outlets as a leading indicator.
insights.locator: The documents obtained by WIRED did not specify

insights.claim: A former chief trial attorney in the CFTC's enforcement division says investigations prompted solely by press reports of potential Commodities Exchange Act violations would be a significant sign of weakness in the regulatory scheme.
insights.speaker: Kate Knibbs
insights.so_what: If the regulator lacks independent market surveillance for event contracts, the gap is an argument for statutory reform — and a latent risk of a sudden, much harsher enforcement regime.
insights.quote: If these investigations are being prompted solely by press reports of potential violations of the Commodities Exchange Act, that’s a significant sign of weakness in this regulatory scheme
insights.locator: If these investigations are being prompted

insights.claim: The CFTC has come under fire in the second Trump era for its perceived friendliness toward the prediction market industry, framing the enforcement record as politically contested rather than routine.
insights.speaker: Kate Knibbs
insights.so_what: A regulator seen as captured is vulnerable to an abrupt reversal under a different administration — a policy-regime risk that is not priced into prediction-market valuations.
insights.locator: The agency has come under fire

insights.claim: The investigation orders granted the enforcement division power to take testimony, obtain subpoenas, administer oaths and require the production of documents, meaning these are full compulsory-process probes rather than informal inquiries.
insights.speaker: Kate Knibbs
insights.so_what: Subpoena authority means counterparties and the exchange itself face document-production burdens now, well before any public charging decision.
insights.locator: The order granted permission to take testimony

insights.claim: A network of suspicious Polymarket accounts made $2.4 million on Iran-related trades with a 98 percent win rate, according to a 60 Minutes report that preceded the CFTC's Iran investigation.
insights.speaker: Kate Knibbs
insights.so_what: A 98 percent win rate on geopolitical contracts is statistically self-incriminating and signals that war-outcome markets attract information asymmetry that exchanges cannot police.
insights.locator: it came two weeks after 60 Minutes aired a report

insights.claim: A trader netted over $300,000 by correctly wagering that Biden would issue preemptive pardons to prominent MAGA critics including Liz Cheney, Adam Kinzinger and Adam Schiff in the final days of his administration.
insights.speaker: Kate Knibbs
insights.so_what: Political-insider leakage into event contracts is the specific abuse most likely to draw congressional attention and a ban on certain contract categories.
insights.locator: the order came several weeks after an NPR report

insights.claim: Federal authorities arrested a US special forces officer in April who prosecutors say used classified information to make more than $400,000 on event contracts tied to the capture of former Venezuelan leader Nicolás Maduro.
insights.speaker: Kate Knibbs
insights.so_what: Classified information being monetized on a public market is a national-security framing that can justify restricting geopolitical event contracts entirely.
insights.locator: So far, two arrests have been made

insights.claim: Google engineer Michele Spagnuolo, who allegedly made over $1.2 million on insider trades, was arrested in May while traveling to New York, with the CFTC filing civil charges and the DOJ filing criminal fraud charges.
insights.speaker: Kate Knibbs
insights.so_what: Corporate employees trading on their own employer's unreleased data creates a new insider-trading compliance obligation for any company whose announcements become tradeable contracts.
insights.locator: And in May, Spagnuolo, who allegedly made over $1.2 million

insights.claim: The CFTC's newest Google-themed probe targets additional individuals beyond Spagnuolo, and the acting enforcement director noted the Southern District of New York is running a parallel investigation.
insights.speaker: Kate Knibbs
insights.so_what: Widening from one defendant to a group plus a parallel SDNY criminal track means the Google matter is escalating, not resolving.
insights.quote: additional individuals who may have engaged in insider trading related to Google’s 2025 Year in Search Ranking
insights.locator: In July, Selig greenlit a third investigation

themes.theme: Legal theory risk: betting vs commodities

insights.claim: Both arrested traders are defending themselves by arguing that Polymarket trades are a form of betting and not subject to commodities law, putting the CFTC's entire jurisdiction over event contracts in play.
insights.speaker: Kate Knibbs
insights.so_what: A ruling that event contracts are gambling would strip CFTC oversight and hand regulation to state gaming authorities — an existential fork for prediction-market business models.
insights.locator: Both men are fighting back by arguing

insights.claim: A former CFTC staffer says parallel criminal investigations into the Iran War and Biden pardon contracts are likely given the significance of the matters, even though the DOJ has not confirmed any.
insights.speaker: Kate Knibbs
insights.so_what: Criminal exposure alongside civil charges raises the cost of trading on these venues for institutional participants and deters professional liquidity provision.
insights.locator: A former CFTC staffer tells WIRED

insights.claim: Polymarket, whose flagship platform was banned from the United States in 2022 and permitted to launch a narrower US-regulated version in late 2025, recently raised a round led by Donald Trump Jr.'s 1789 Capital at a $21 billion valuation.
insights.speaker: Kate Knibbs
insights.so_what: A $21 billion mark on a platform under active regulatory investigation, funded by a politically connected vehicle, makes valuation contingent on the political configuration persisting.
insights.locator: The CFTC is also reportedly investigating Polymarket itself

insights.claim: Polymarket's deputy chief legal officer says the company regularly refers matters to law enforcement and supports ongoing investigations as part of protecting market integrity, positioning the exchange as a cooperating party rather than a target.
insights.speaker: Kate Knibbs
insights.so_what: Self-referral is the standard playbook for venues seeking to stay on the regulator's good side while individual traders absorb liability — watch whether it holds as the CFTC probes the company itself.
insights.quote: we regularly refer matters to law enforcement and support ongoing investigations as part of our commitment to protecting the integrity of our markets
insights.locator: While we do not comment on specific investigations

insights.claim: Rival Kalshi has referred at least 32 cases to the CFTC, a far more systematic self-policing record than anything documented for Polymarket.
insights.speaker: Kate Knibbs
insights.so_what: Compliance posture is becoming a competitive differentiator between prediction-market venues and will likely determine which survives an enforcement crackdown.
insights.locator: The CFTC has also launched investigations into potential insider trading on Kalshi

insights.claim: The CFTC fined former US representative George Santos $35,000 over a Kalshi contract on whether he would attend Trump's 2026 State of the Union address, while Kalshi separately issued its first-ever lifetime ban and a fine of just over $71,000, and Santos faced no criminal charges.
insights.speaker: Kate Knibbs
insights.so_what: The exchange's private penalty exceeded the regulator's fine, showing venue self-enforcement is currently the sharper deterrent — and a template regulators may formalize.
insights.locator: The CFTC fined former US representative George Santos
